newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fokker receivers hope for sale news on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Fokker receivers hope for sale news on Tuesday.

text.p: The administrators of bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV hope there will be developments on Tuesday in talks on the company's sale, a spokesman said on Monday.
"I don't expect any developments today. I hope there will be developments tomorrow," Ben Knueppe, a spokesman for the court appointed administrators, told Reuters.

But he denied media reports that agreement had already been reached between South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries, the only serious candidate to buy Fokker, and the Dutch government on the terms of a takeover.
Samsung Aerospace earlier denied it had reached agreement with the government on the terms of a takeover, saying it was still negotiating and differences remained.
Dutch television reported on Sunday that negotiators had reached broad agreement on Friday, but the government said later the same day it was unaware of such a deal.
Fokker collapsed and went bankrupt on March 15, two months after its German parent Daimler Benz Aerospace cut vital credit lines in response to Fokker's huge losses.
It has been kept alive since then by its administrators.
Under the business plan presented earlier this month, Samsung wants the Dutch government to take a minority stake in the new Fokker and provide large subsidies.
The administrators have previously told Fokker's staff that the deadline for a rescue plan is the end of this month.
A successful rescue depends on the purchase price, the establishment of a new aircraft leasing company and loans to develop a new 125-seat aircraft, larger than the company's current range of jets.
